Worker in a git worktree of the Fortress revival repo. Mission: implement `explorations/microgpt_paper.fss` (component `microgpt_paper`) — the paper-register rewrite — to a fixed spec, and produce its Fortify render sheet.

Setup: env + build per CLAUDE.md build section, FORTRESS_HOME=$PWD (your worktree), `ant compileAll` once, then smoke-test `FORTRESS_THREADS=1 ./bin/fortress explorations/mgnative_a.fss` (must PASS, ~30 s).

Instruction by reference — read in order:
1. explorations/microgpt-native.md, section "Course correction: the paper register" — points 1–6 are your spec, verbatim.
2. explorations/microgpt_native.fss — your starting point: copy it and transform. The autodiff engine, BIG OPLUS machinery, golden check values, tokenizer, Adam, training loop, and sampling carry over; what changes is the notation layer (new vector/matrix operators per spec point 2) and the model-level definitions (spec point 3). Heads stay structural (head-indexed wq/wk/wv), histories stay functionally threaded.
3. explorations/microgpt-native-brief.md, "Process & repo conventions" — the syntax-trap list; also the two new traps in explorations/microgpt-native-impl-report.md ("Syntax traps hit"): chained subscripts need `(m[i])[j]`, comprehension bodies ending in a subscript need parens, list-literal type ascriptions are load-bearing.

Notes for the new operators: `opr DOT(u: List[\V\], v: List[\V\]): V` as an ⊕-comprehension; vector-times-matrix `opr juxtaposition(p: List[\V\], m: List[\List[\V\]\]): List[\V\]` — the overload differs from the existing matrix-times-vector by argument order, both must coexist; scalar-times-vector `opr juxtaposition(a: V, x: List[\V\]): List[\V\]` — watch for overload ambiguity with V-times-V juxtaposition (should be fine, distinct second arg) and test that `p Vv` in expressions resolves to the intended overload. Vector/scalar `opr /`. Elementwise `relu(x: List[\V\])` and, if softmax wants it, `exp` on vectors. `concat(heads: List[\List[\V\]\]): List[\V\]` by the two-generator comprehension. If an overload turns out ambiguous or unparseable, record the failure verbatim and pick the closest working form — the failure itself is a result we want documented.

Gates, in order (FORTRESS_THREADS=1, generous timeouts): (1) goldenCheck PASS at 1e-9 — same hardcoded values as microgpt_native; (2) 30-step nano run, loss ~3.29 declining; (3) timing s/step for comparison with microgpt_native's 4.81 s/step.

Render sheet: write explorations/fortify/microgpt-paper-forms.tic in the exact format of explorations/fortify/microgpt-native-forms.tic (see its header for the 3-command regeneration recipe; run it; also produce the -dark.svg variant by the sed in the repo's practice: sed "s/<svg /<svg fill='#e6edf3' /" light > dark; delete .tex/.dvi/.aux/.log byproducts). Contents: the notation-layer definitions (DOT, the three juxtaposition overloads, vector /, elementwise relu, concat) as one group, then the model-level block definitions (rmsnorm, softmax, attScore or its replacement, attend, ffn if a named definition exists, nll, forward) as a second group. Rasterize the light SVG with `/opt/pw-browsers/chromium --headless --no-sandbox --disable-gpu --screenshot=... --window-size=1500,1600` and LOOK at it: if a definition renders with obvious noise the spec's minimal form avoids, iterate the source (keeping golden green) before delivering.

Discipline: worktree only; no commits or pushes; create only microgpt_paper.fss and the fortify sheet files. Copy deliverables to /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-fortress/bdff267d-67dc-5bb9-b970-8c3dfaa634b6/scratchpad/: microgpt_paper.fss, microgpt-paper-forms.tic, microgpt-paper-forms-light.svg, microgpt-paper-forms-dark.svg, the rasterized PNG, and microgpt_paper-report.md (gates + numbers + every notation contest you had to adjudicate and why + traps hit). Final message: compact summary + paths.

1	# microgpt-native: design journal
2	
3	The documented evolution of `microgpt.fss` from verified transliteration
4	to canonical Fortress. Mission, rules, and grounding:
5	`explorations/microgpt-native-brief.md`. Method: explore alternatives,
6	adjudicate by algorithmic purity (is this the computation, or an
7	accident of implementation?), verify each step against the v1 golden
8	anchors, measure everything, and never declare a form canonical after a
9	first pass.
10	
11	Companion code: `explorations/nprobe.fss` (idiom probes),
12	`explorations/tparallel.fss` (parallelism characterization), and the
13	`microgpt_n*.fss` version ladder as it grows.
14	
15	## 2026-08-24 — Probe results: the 2012 interpreter vs the 2015 idioms
16	
17	The Four Solutions talk postdates our tree's freeze by three years, so
18	before designing anything we probed every idiom the rewrite wants
19	(`nprobe.fss`, run under the walk interpreter, JDK 25 container):
20	
21	| # | Idiom | Verdict |
22	|---|-------|---------|
23	| P1 | `SUM[(p,q) <- pairs] q`, `SUM[v <- xs] v v`, `SUM[k <- 0#4] xs[k]` | **works** — big-operator comprehensions with tuple-destructuring generators, exactly the slides' syntax |
24	| P2 | user monoid: `object WSum extends CommutativeMonoidReduction[\W\]` + `opr BIG OPLUS(): BigReduction[\W,W\]` registration | **works** — `BIG OPLUS[w <- ws] w` reduces a user type through a user join |
25	| P3 | commandeering `SUM` itself for a user type | **impossible** — three ways (below) |
26	| P4 | implicit tuple parallelism `(a,b) = (f p, f q)` | **works** — and exposed the interpreter's performance law (below) |
27	| P5 | `trait Tree comprises {…}` + multimethod structural recursion | **works** |
28	| P6 | `atomic do … end` | **works** — ~16% overhead over a plain assignment in a hot loop (≈2 µs/op); cheap enough to consider for parallel gradient accumulation |
29	| P7 | `zip` inside a comprehension: `SUM[(a,b) <- xs.zip[\RR64\](ys)] a b` | **works** (explicit type arg needed on `zip`) |
30	| P8 | `xs.split()` | **works** — `(<\|1,2\|>, <\|3,4\|>)` |
31	
32	So the full Steele register is available to us, with one closed door:
33	
34	**P3, why `SUM` is closed.** Library `SUM` is
35	`opr SUM[\T extends Number\]()` and `Number comprises {RR64}` — sealed,
36	so an autodiff `V` can never satisfy the bound. Overloading is also out:
37	a nullary `opr SUM()` of our own collides ("parameter lists have the
38	same types" — the check ignores static params, tested with a
39	disjoint-bound generic too), and a generator-only overload
40	`opr SUM(g: Generator[\V\])` is bypassed because the comprehension
41	desugars through the *nullary* form, then dies casting `V` to `Number`.
42	Consequence: reductions over `V` use a **registered user BIG operator**.
43	Which glyph to use is a real design decision, deferred to the value-type
44	design below (Steele's own precedent for a user monoid is `BIG OPLUS`,
45	but ⊕ is not the papers' Σ; an n-ary sum *node* may dissolve the
46	question entirely).
47	
48	## 2026-08-24 — The interpreter's performance law (found, not sought)
49	
50	P4's numbers made no sense at first: on a 4-CPU box (interpreter pool =
51	`floor(cpus/2)` = 2 workers, override `FORTRESS_THREADS`), a 500k-iter
52	scalar loop took 12–14 s run bare, but **two** of them inside a tuple
53	finished in 2.6 s — an "impossible" 8× from a 2-way fork. A tuple with
54	only one nontrivial element stayed slow, so it wasn't a fast task path.
55	`tparallel.fss` isolates it:
56	
57	| shape | 2 workers | 1 worker |
58	|-------|----------:|---------:|
59	| one loop, bare | 11.9–13.6 s | **2.1 s** |
60	| 2-tuple of loops | 2.6 s | 4.2 s |
61	| 4-tuple of loops | 5.4 s | 9.1 s |
62	| `(loop, 0)` tuple | 14.4 s | 2.2 s |
63	
64	Mechanism (from `BaseTask.worthSpawning()` /
65	`TupleTask.worthSpawning()`, runtime source): everything runs inside the
66	fork-join pool, and the evaluator considers forking operand pairs of
67	ordinary expressions whenever the surplus-task count is low. With idle
68	workers it therefore **micro-forks constantly** — the 21 s of *kernel*
69	time below is that churn — and per-op cost is ~6× the inline path. Once
70	every worker is saturated (or with `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, which never
71	spawns), evaluation goes inline and fast. Saturated 2-worker scaling is
72	real: 2.6 s vs 4.2 s single-worker = 1.6× on 2 workers.
73	
74	Checked against real v1 code — `micrograd.fss` XOR training, results
75	bit-identical both ways: 45.2 s wall (21.7 s sys) default vs **19.8 s
76	wall (0.5 s sys)** with `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`.
77	
78	Consequences for this project:
79	
80	- Every mgbench/v1 number we published was measured on the pathological
81	  middle ground (2 workers, unsaturated): v1's 10.9 s/step is not the
82	  interpreter's floor. Re-baseline v1 under `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` before
83	  comparing native versions against it.
84	- The native version's parallelism must come in **coarse grains** that
85	  saturate the pool (Steele's "sequential at the leaves" is also the
86	  fast path here); fine-grained implicit forking is exactly what the
87	  slow path is made of.
88	- This is slide 91 measurable in Steele's own interpreter: "the
89	  overheads are real … and will shrink but not disappear."
90	
91	## Design questions now open
92	
93	1. **The value type.** Keep Karpathy's binary-graph `V` (children +
94	   local grads) vs an autodiff whose *sum is n-ary* — a `Sum` node with
95	   all addends as children, local grads 1 — which is arguably the Σ of
96	   the papers rather than a left-fold accident. Explore both.
97	2. **The reduction glyph for V.** `BIG OPLUS` (Steele's user-monoid
98	   precedent) vs dissolving V-level Σ into an n-ary node constructor.
99	   Fortify rendering is part of the fitness function.
100	3. **Backward pass.** v1's `visited` flag + explicit `Topo` object is
101	   one implementation of reverse-topological order. Alternatives:
102	   `comprises`-ADT multimethod walk (P5), commutative-monoid gradient
103	   accumulation, `atomic` accumulation under parallel construction (P6).
104	   Parallel *construction* of the graph is pure; parallel *backward*
105	   races on `grad` — a design question, not a reason for global `seq`.
106	4. **Formulation level.** Decided in the brief: per-token index
107	   formulas (what the program computes, KV cache included), papers'
108	   notation. Each formula should be one Fortress definition whose
109	   Fortify rendering approximates it.
110	
111	Next: micrograd-scale value-type alternatives (question 1), verified
112	against v1's analytic derivatives and the XOR trajectory.
113	
114	## 2026-08-24 — Surface notation probes (P9–P11)
115	
116	Before designing the value type, three more probes (added to
117	`nprobe.fss`): a user type can carry **`opr juxtaposition`** (so `q k`
118	multiplies two autodiff values the way the papers juxtapose q_m k_m),
119	**`opr ^(self, n: RR64)`**, and unary `opr -`; and the library's prefix
120	functions **`exp`/`log` can be overloaded** for a user type (plain
121	function overloading — unlike `SUM`, nothing collides). All work. The
122	papers' surface register is therefore fully available: the only
123	substitution forced on us is ⊕ where a paper writes Σ over graph values
124	(and Σ proper still applies wherever the summands are `Number`s — which
125	the backward pass will exploit).
126	
127	One more table fact: ∑ (U+2211) is a hard alias of `SUM`, and ∇
128	(U+2207) is not a Fortress operator at all, but **∂ (U+2202) is `DEL`**
129	— free for user definition. Both remaining alternatives below use it.
130	
131	## 2026-08-24 — The value type: three alternatives, built and measured
132	
133	All three share the decisions already made: papers' surface notation;
134	summation as an **n-ary Sum node** whose ∂ to every addend is 1, built
135	by `BIG OPLUS` over a *list-concatenation* monoid (`Comprehension`'s
136	`body` maps each addend to a singleton, `join` concatenates — exactly
137	associative, so parallel construction cannot perturb anything — and
138	`unwrap` lifts the addend list into one node whose value is the single
139	sequential fold, in generator order, at the leaf: Steele's "map to
140	singletons, merge treewise" and "sequential at the leaves" in one
141	object). All three run the same harness as v1 `micrograd.fss`: analytic
142	gradient checks at 1e-12 plus the XOR MLP, whose network is now one
143	definition:
144	
145	    yhat(xa, xb) = b2v + (BIG OPLUS[j <- 0#nH] w2[j] relu(xa w1[j] + xb w1[nH+j] + b1[j]))
146	
147	and whose whole SGD bookkeeping is one loop over a `params` list (v1
148	needed ten lines of per-array bookkeeping).
149	
150	**A — uniform tape** (`mgnative_a.fss`): v1's node — children plus
151	local-gradient lists cached at construction — under the new surface.
152	The chain rule doesn't care which operation made a node, only what its
153	∂-values are; the uniform node is that observation as a data structure
154	(the Wengert-tape view).
155	
156	**B — sealed ADT** (`mgnative_b.fss`): `trait Ex comprises {Leaf, Plus,
157	Times, Neg, Pow, Exp, Log, Relu, Sum}`, the symbolic-expression view.
158	The derivative table becomes nine visible equations, multimethods on
159	the prefix operator ∂:
160	
161	    opr DEL(e: Times): List[\RR64\] = <|[\RR64\] e.b.data, e.a.data|>
162	    opr DEL(e: Exp):   List[\RR64\] = <|[\RR64\] e.data|>
163	
164	Mutation is quarantined in a `Cell` composed into each node (traits
165	cannot hold fields; abstract setters have no precedent in the 2012
166	tree — the Cell is both the workaround and arguably the cleaner
167	statement: nodes immutable, accumulator explicit). Subtlety recorded:
168	B *recomputes* ∂ from `data` at backward time, so it is only correct
169	while forward values are unmutated; A and C snapshot ∂ at construction
170	and are robust to interleaved parameter updates.
171	
172	**C — adjoint recursion** (`mgnative_c.fss`): the mathematically
173	explicit backward. The tape stores only the *transpose* graph (each new
174	node registers `(node, ∂node/∂child)` with its children), and the
175	gradient is the memoized literal chain rule — a genuine Σ-comprehension,
176	since adjoints are `Number`s:
177	
178	    opr DEL(v: V): RR64 =   (* memoized *)
179	      if |v.outs| = 0 then 1.0                        (* dL/dL = 1 *)
180	      else SUM[(u,d) <- seq(v.outs)] (DEL u) d end
181	
182	No topological sort, no visited flags, no zero-then-accumulate sweep —
183	"first, SUM = 0 you are hosed" eliminated from the backward pass
184	itself. The SGD update reads `q.data := q.data - lr (DEL q)`.
185	Trade-offs: out-edge registration mutates the *children* at
186	construction, which is the one obstacle to parallel graph building
187	(atomic would fix it — P6 measured that cheap); and the recursion depth
188	is the graph depth.
189	
190	**Results** (400 XOR epochs, `FORTRESS_THREADS=1`): every alternative
191	reproduces every printed loss of every other **bit-for-bit** (final
192	5.5178095183714354E-11), despite three different backward orders — one
193	arithmetic, three representations. Against v1 (5.51780951879265E-11)

240	## 2026-08-24 — Architecture of the transformer-scale rewrite
241	
242	Working mode from here (Pavol's direction): experiments and
243	implementation are delegated to workers; this journal carries the
244	design decisions and their reasons. In parallel, a worker is
245	characterizing which of our sources the **bytecode compiler** path
246	accepts — both for possible speedups and to ground a catalog of
247	compiler gaps in real programs.
248	
249	Decisions for `microgpt_native.fss` (engine = alternative A):
250	
251	1. **Vectors are `List[\V\]`, matrices lists of row-vectors, and every
252	   reduction is a scalar-level ⊕ comprehension.** No `Vec`/`Mat`
253	   objects, no vector-sum monoid. Reason: the chosen canonical level is
254	   the papers' per-token *index* formulas (`A_ij = (Σ_m Q_im K_jm)/√d_k`),
255	   which are scalar-Σ statements already; and a second `BIG OPLUS`
256	   registration for a vector carrier would collide with the scalar one
257	   (nullary big-operator registrations are one-per-name — the P3
258	   lesson). `(W x)_r = ⊕_m W[r][m] x[m]` is one comprehension inside a
259	   list comprehension.
260	2. **Heads are structure, not offsets** (purity ledger). `wq/wk/wv` are
261	   head-indexed lists of (hs × d) matrices, per-head caches of
262	   hs-vectors; the flat d×d matrix and its offset arithmetic
263	   (`h headDim + m`) disappear. Golden-check preservation constraint:
264	   the deterministic init formula must be evaluated at the *global* row
265	   index (head h, row m → row h·hs+m of v1's flat matrix) so the
266	   partitioned weights are value-identical to v1's — a row-block
267	   partition of the same matvec.
268	3. **There is no "cache".** In the autoregressive index formulas the
269	   attention at step i sums over k_j, v_j for j ≤ i; the growing lists
270	   `keys`/`vals` ARE those formulas' data, not a memo of something
271	   else. (Adjudicates the KV-cache ledger entry: at this formulation
272	   level it is not an optimization at all.)
273	4. **Division becomes a primitive**: `opr /(V,V)` with ∂ = (1/b, −a/b²)
274	   and `opr /(V, RR64)` for constant divisors (√d_k), replacing v1's
275	   pow(−1)-then-multiply — the formulas say division.
276	5. **Softmax keeps the max-shift** with the shift as an RR64 constant
277	   (softmax(x) = softmax(x−c) identity; ledger: legitimate), written
278	   inside one `softmax(List[\V\]): List[\V\]` definition; the loss is
279	   `−log softmax(logits)[y]`.
280	6. **Adam stays index-form RR64 arithmetic** over a flat parameter
281	   list with parallel m/v arrays — the optimizer's equations are
282	   already scalar index formulas.

284	   reordering drift is ~1e-15 relative), then a short nano training
285	   run confirming the loss decline from ~3.29, then timing under
286	   `FORTRESS_THREADS=1` and default (2 workers), against v1
287	   re-baselined the same way.

289	   correctness: heads and matvec rows are independent (pure graph
290	   construction under engine A), the backward sweep stays sequential
291	   for now; C's per-node Σ remains the candidate for a parallel
292	   backward later.

362	the chart (`prng-chart.svg`). Summary: Fortress's `random()` is
363	literally `Math.random()` — one process-wide time-seeded `java.util.Random`,
364	unseedable from Fortress source — yet swapping it for CPython's Mersenne
365	Twister changes nothing observable: the two Box–Müller samplers are
366	statistically indistinguishable at our sizes, and the three Fortress
367	trajectories sit inside the 15-seed CPython envelope at exactly the rate
368	a 16th seed would (tail means 0.03 sd apart). The v1 loss-band anchor

371	Two consequences adopted:
372	
373	- **Correction filed** in `microgpt-port.md`: its premise "Python's
374	  Mersenne Twister is not ours" was wrong — `Library/Random.fss` ships

427

429	project, not the transformer, and it showed one notation carried up a
430	ladder rather than a genuine exploration of notational alternatives.

441	earlier (per-token index formulas): the literature's register for the
442	model level is **vector/matrix notation** — `softmax(q·Kᵀ/√d_k)V`,

import List.{...}
export Executable

object V(var data: RR64, children: List[\V\], grads: List[\RR64\])
  var grad: RR64 := 0.0
  var visited: Boolean := false
  opr +(self, o: V): V = V(data + o.data, <|[\V\] self, o|>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0, 1.0|>)
  opr juxtaposition(self, o: V): V =
    V(data o.data, <|[\V\] self, o|>, <|[\RR64\] o.data, data|>)
  opr -(self): V = V(-data, <|[\V\] self|>, <|[\RR64\] -1.0|>)
  opr -(self, o: V): V = self + (-o)
  opr /(self, o: V): V =
    V(data / o.data, <|[\V\] self, o|>,
      <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / o.data, (-data) / (o.data o.data)|>)
  opr /(self, c: RR64): V = V(data / c, <|[\V\] self|>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / c|>)
  opr ^(self, n: RR64): V = V(data^n, <|[\V\] self|>, <|[\RR64\] n data^(n-1.0)|>)
end

konst(d: RR64): V = V(d, emptyList[\V\](), emptyList[\RR64\]())
exp(v: V): V = V(exp v.data, <|[\V\] v|>, <|[\RR64\] exp v.data|>)
relu(v: V): V = if v.data > 0.0
                then V(v.data, <|[\V\] v|>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0|>)
                else V(0.0, <|[\V\] v|>, <|[\RR64\] 0.0|>) end

vsum(addends: List[\V\]): V =
  V(SUM[a <- seq(addends)] a.data, addends, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 | a <- addends|>)

object VConcat extends MonoidReduction[\List[\V\]\]
  getter asString(): String = "VConcat"
  empty(): List[\V\] = emptyList[\V\]()
  join(a: List[\V\], b: List[\V\]): List[\V\] = a || b
end

opr BIG OPLUS(): Comprehension[\V,V,List[\V\],List[\V\]\] =
  Comprehension[\V,V,List[\V\],List[\V\]\](fn l => vsum(l), VConcat,
                                           fn v => singleton[\V\](v))
opr BIG OPLUS(g: Generator[\V\]): V =
  __bigOperatorSugar[\V,V,List[\V\],List[\V\]\](BIG OPLUS(), g)

(* ---- probes ---- *)

opr DOT(u: List[\V\], v: List[\V\]): V = BIG OPLUS[m <- 0#|u|] (u[m] v[m])

opr juxtaposition(w: List[\List[\V\]\], x: List[\V\]): List[\V\] =
  <|[\V\] (BIG OPLUS[m <- 0#|x|] (w[r])[m] x[m]) | r <- 0#|w||>

opr juxtaposition(p: List[\V\], m: List[\List[\V\]\]): List[\V\] =
  <|[\V\] (BIG OPLUS[j <- 0#|p|] p[j] ((m[j])[c])) | c <- 0#|m[0]||>

opr juxtaposition(a: V, x: List[\V\]): List[\V\] = <|[\V\] (a u) | u <- x|>

opr +(a: List[\V\], b: List[\V\]): List[\V\] =
  <|[\V\] (p + q) | (p, q) <- a.zip[\V\](b)|>

opr -(x: List[\V\], c: V): List[\V\] = <|[\V\] (u - c) | u <- x|>

opr /(x: List[\V\], s: V): List[\V\] = <|[\V\] (u / s) | u <- x|>

opr /(x: List[\V\], c: RR64): List[\V\] = <|[\V\] (u / c) | u <- x|>

relu(x: List[\V\]): List[\V\] = <|[\V\] (relu u) | u <- x|>

exp(x: List[\V\]): List[\V\] = <|[\V\] (exp u) | u <- x|>

concat(heads: List[\List[\V\]\]): List[\V\] = <|[\V\] u | h <- heads, u <- h|>

softmax(a: List[\V\]): List[\V\] = do
  c = konst(BIG MAX[u <- seq(a)] u.data)
  e = exp(a - c)
  e / (BIG OPLUS[u <- e] u)
end

rmsnorm(x: List[\V\]): List[\V\] = do
  d = |x|
  x / (((x DOT x) / (d 1.0) + konst(0.00001))^0.5)
end

attend(q: List[\V\], K: List[\List[\V\]\], Vv: List[\List[\V\]\]): List[\V\] = do
  dk = |q|
  softmax(<|[\V\] ((q DOT k) / SQRT (dk 1.0)) | k <- K|>) Vv
end

vec(xs: List[\RR64\]): List[\V\] = <|[\V\] (konst u) | u <- xs|>

run() = do
  a = vec(<|[\RR64\] 1.0, 2.0, 3.0|>)
  b = vec(<|[\RR64\] 4.0, 5.0, 6.0|>)
  println("DOT = " (a DOT b).data)
  w = <|[\List[\V\]\] a, b|>
  println("(w a)_0 = " ((w a)[0]).data " (w a)_1 = " ((w a)[1]).data)
  p = vec(<|[\RR64\] 2.0, 3.0|>)
  pm = p w
  println("(p w) = " (pm[0]).data " " (pm[1]).data " " (pm[2]).data)
  s = konst(10.0)
  sa = s a
  println("(s a)_2 = " (sa[2]).data)
  ab = a + b
  println("(a+b)_0 = " (ab[0]).data)
  am = a - s
  println("(a-s)_0 = " (am[0]).data)
  ad = a / s
  println("(a/s)_0 = " (ad[0]).data)
  ac = a / 2.0
  println("(a/2)_0 = " (ac[0]).data)
  ra = relu(a - s)
  println("relu_0 = " (ra[0]).data)
  ea = exp(a)
  println("exp_0 = " (ea[0]).data)
  cc = concat(<|[\List[\V\]\] a, b|>)
  println("concat = " |cc| " first " (cc[0]).data " last " (cc[5]).data)
  sm = softmax(a)
  println("softmax = " (sm[0]).data " " (sm[1]).data " " (sm[2]).data)
  rn = rmsnorm(a)
  println("rmsnorm_0 = " (rn[0]).data)
  at = attend(a, <|[\List[\V\]\] a, b|>, <|[\List[\V\]\] a, b|>)
  println("attend = " (at[0]).data " " (at[1]).data " " (at[2]).data)
end
end

import File.{...}
export Executable

(* microgpt_paper.fss -- the paper-register rewrite of
   explorations/microgpt_native.fss (which stays in-tree as the index-form
   rung of the notation ladder: transliteration -> index formulas -> paper
   register).  Spec and reasons: explorations/microgpt-native.md, section
   "Course correction: the paper register".

   The literature states the model level in vector/matrix notation --
   softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k) V, W_2 relu(W_1 x), x / SQRT(x.x/d + eps) --
   and the index formulas are one level DOWN, as the definitions of that
   notation.  So this file is in two layers:

     - a NOTATION LAYER, each operator defined once by its index formula
       (these definitions are themselves the exhibits: they are what
       Fortress has to be taught before the model level can be stated);
     - a MODEL LEVEL, where each block of the transformer is one
       paper-shaped line over those operators.

   The autodiff engine (alternative A: a uniform tape node, summation as an
   n-ary Sum node built by BIG OPLUS over a list-concatenation monoid),
   the tokenizer, Adam, the training loop and the sampling loop carry over
   from microgpt_native.fss unchanged.  Adam stays index-form RR64
   arithmetic on purpose: its literature form IS elementwise index
   arithmetic, and the contrast with the model level is a teaching point.

   Verified: v1's goldenCheck numbers at 1e-9, then a nano training run. *)

(* ---------- scalar reverse-mode autodiff ---------- *)

object V(var data: RR64, children: List[\V\], grads: List[\RR64\])
  var grad: RR64 := 0.0
  var visited: Boolean := false
  opr +(self, o: V): V = V(data + o.data, <|[\V\] self, o|>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0, 1.0|>)
  opr +(self, c: RR64): V = V(data + c, <|[\V\] self|>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0|>)
  opr juxtaposition(self, o: V): V =
    V(data o.data, <|[\V\] self, o|>, <|[\RR64\] o.data, data|>)
  opr -(self): V = V(-data, <|[\V\] self|>, <|[\RR64\] -1.0|>)
  opr -(self, o: V): V = self + (-o)
  opr /(self, o: V): V =
    V(data / o.data, <|[\V\] self, o|>,
      <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / o.data, (-data) / (o.data o.data)|>)
  opr /(self, c: RR64): V = V(data / c, <|[\V\] self|>, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 / c|>)
  opr /(self, n: ZZ32): V = self / (n 1.0)
  opr ^(self, n: RR64): V = V(data^n, <|[\V\] self|>, <|[\RR64\] n data^(n-1.0)|>)
end

konst(d: RR64): V = V(d, emptyList[\V\](), emptyList[\RR64\]())

exp(v: V): V = V(exp v.data, <|[\V\] v|>, <|[\RR64\] exp v.data|>)

                else V(0.0, <|[\V\] v|>, <|[\RR64\] 0.0|>) end

opr SQRT(u: V): V = u^0.5
opr SQRT(n: ZZ32): RR64 = SQRT (n 1.0)

(* n-ary summation node: d(Sum)/d(addend_i) = 1.  The forward value is the one
   sequential fold, in list order, at the leaf. *)
vsum(addends: List[\V\]): V =
  V(SUM[a <- seq(addends)] a.data, addends, <|[\RR64\] 1.0 | a <- addends|>)

   concatenation (exactly associative -- parallel construction cannot perturb
   the result), lift the addend list into one Sum node. *)
object VConcat extends MonoidReduction[\List[\V\]\]
  getter asString(): String = "VConcat"
  empty(): List[\V\] = emptyList[\V\]()
  join(a: List[\V\], b: List[\V\]): List[\V\] = a || b
end

                                           fn v => singleton[\V\](v))
opr BIG OPLUS(g: Generator[\V\]): V =
  __bigOperatorSugar[\V,V,List[\V\],List[\V\]\](BIG OPLUS(), g)

object Topo()
  var items: List[\V\] := emptyList[\V\]()
  build(v: V): () = do
    if NOT v.visited then
      v.visited := true
      for ch <- seq(v.children) do self.build(ch) end
      items := items.addRight(v)
    end
  end
end

  root.grad := 1.0

(* ---------- the notation layer ---------- *)

(* Vectors are List[\V\], matrices lists of row-vectors; no wrapper objects,

(* attention at one step: p = softmax(q K^T / SQRT d_k),  out = SUM_j p_j V_j.
   K and Vv are the key/value vectors of positions 0..i, so the causal mask is
   the data, not a mask. *)
attend(q: List[\V\], K: List[\List[\V\]\], Vv: List[\List[\V\]\]): List[\V\] = do
  p = softmax(<|[\V\] ((q DOT k) / SQRT |q|) | k <- K|>)
  BIG BOXPLUS[j <- 0#|p|] p[j] Vv[j]
end

(* L = -log softmax(logits)_y *)
nll(logits: List[\V\], y: ZZ32): V = -(log ((softmax(logits))[y]))

(* one layer, nHead heads; n_layer = 1 as in Karpathy's default.  kh/vh are the
   per-head histories of key/value vectors for positions 0..i-1; forward returns
   the logits together with the histories extended by position i. *)
object Model(vocab: ZZ32, nEmbd: ZZ32, nHead: ZZ32, headSize: ZZ32,
             wte: List[\List[\V\]\], wpe: List[\List[\V\]\], lmHead: List[\List[\V\]\],
             wq: List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\], wk: List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\],
             wv: List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\],
             wo: List[\List[\V\]\], fc1: List[\List[\V\]\], fc2: List[\List[\V\]\])

  (* FFN(x) = W_2 relu(W_1 x) *)
  ffn(x: List[\V\]): List[\V\] = fc2 relu(fc1 x)

  forward(t: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, kh: List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\], vh: List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\]): (List[\V\], List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\], List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\]) = do
    h0 = wte[t] + wpe[i]
    x1 = rmsnorm(h0)
    x2 = rmsnorm(x1)
    kh2 = <|[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] ((kh[h]).addRight(wk[h] x2)) | h <- 0#nHead|>
    vh2 = <|[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] ((vh[h]).addRight(wv[h] x2)) | h <- 0#nHead|>
    heads = <|[\List[\V\]\] (attend(wq[h] x2, kh2[h], vh2[h])) | h <- 0#nHead|>
    x4 = wo concat(heads) + x1
    x5 = rmsnorm(x4)
    x6 = ffn(x5) + x4
    (lmHead x6, kh2, vh2)
  end
end

emptyHist(nh: ZZ32): List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] =
  <|[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] (emptyList[\List[\V\]\]()) | h <- 0#nh|>

(* ---------- weights ---------- *)

(* deterministic weights for the golden check (no RNG; the same formula lives in
   the Python reference generator).  goldRows(mi, r0, rows, cols) is the row
   block r0 .. r0+rows-1 of v1's flat matrix mi -- so a head's slice carries
   exactly v1's values. *)
initW(i: ZZ32, j: ZZ32): RR64 = (((31 i + 17 j) REM 97) - 48) / 100.0

goldRow(mi: ZZ32, i: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): List[\V\] =
  <|[\V\] (konst(initW(100 mi + i, j))) | j <- 0#cols|>

goldRows(mi: ZZ32, r0: ZZ32, rows: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): List[\List[\V\]\] =
  <|[\List[\V\]\] (goldRow(mi, r0 + i, cols)) | i <- 0#rows|>

goldMat(mi: ZZ32, rows: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): List[\List[\V\]\] =
  goldRows(mi, 0, rows, cols)

goldHeads(mi: ZZ32, nh: ZZ32, hs: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32): List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] =
  <|[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] (goldRows(mi, h hs, hs, cols)) | h <- 0#nh|>

(* Box-Muller; random() is the library native *)
gauss(std: RR64): RR64 = do
  var u1: RR64 := random(1.0)
  if u1 < 0.000000000001 then u1 := 0.000000000001 end
  u2 = random(1.0)
  r = SQRT (-2.0 (log u1))
  theta = 2.0 3.141592653589793 u2
  std r (cos theta)
end

gaussRow(cols: ZZ32, std: RR64): List[\V\] =
  <|[\V\] (konst(gauss(std))) | j <- 0#cols|>

gaussMat(rows: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32, std: RR64): List[\List[\V\]\] =
  <|[\List[\V\]\] (gaussRow(cols, std)) | i <- 0#rows|>

gaussHeads(nh: ZZ32, hs: ZZ32, cols: ZZ32, std: RR64): List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] =
  <|[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] (gaussMat(hs, cols, std)) | h <- 0#nh|>

  hs: ZZ32 = 2
  g = Model(5, 4, nH, hs,
            goldMat(0, 5, 4), goldMat(1, 4, 4), goldMat(2, 5, 4),
            goldHeads(3, nH, hs, 4), goldHeads(4, nH, hs, 4), goldHeads(5, nH, hs, 4),
            goldMat(6, 4, 4), goldMat(7, 16, 4), goldMat(8, 4, 16))
  tol = 10.0^(-9)
  tokens = <|[\ZZ32\] 4, 0, 1, 4|>
  gold0 = <|[\RR64\] 1.1786640480869652, 0.08369680205708685, -1.2116330341802932, 1.161464590811486, 0.06649734478160751|>
  gold1 = <|[\RR64\] -0.5153754312822434, 0.7583368418857922, -0.6709093810270941, -0.44385589510170814, 0.8298563780663275|>

  assert(|(glm[2])[3].grad - 0.028373522248445866| < tol, "grad lm_head[2][3]")

            gaussMat(vocab, nEmbd, 0.08), gaussMat(blockSize, nEmbd, 0.08),
            gaussMat(vocab, nEmbd, 0.08),

            gaussHeads(nHead, hs, nEmbd, 0.08),
            gaussMat(nEmbd, nEmbd, 0.08), gaussMat(4 nEmbd, nEmbd, 0.08),
            gaussMat(nEmbd, 4 nEmbd, 0.08))

  var psL: List[\V\] := emptyList[\V\]()
  for m <- seq(<|[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] g.wte, g.wpe, g.lmHead, g.wo, g.fc1, g.fc2|>) do
    for row <- seq(m) do

    for m <- seq(hm) do

    end

  params = array[\V\](nP).fill(fn (i: ZZ32) => psL[i])
  println("num params: " nP)

  mBuf = array[\RR64\](nP).fill(fn (i: ZZ32) => 0.0)
  vBuf = array[\RR64\](nP).fill(fn (i: ZZ32) => 0.0)

  t0 = nanoTime()
  for step <- seq(0#numSteps) do
    doc = docs[step REM |docs|]
    len: ZZ32 = |doc|
    toks = array[\ZZ32\](len + 2).fill(fn (i: ZZ32) =>
      if i = 0 OR i = len + 1 then bos else doc[i - 1].codePoint() - 97 end)

    var vh: List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] := emptyHist(nHead)
    var losses: List[\V\] := emptyList[\V\]()
    for pos <- seq(0#n) do
      (logits, kh2, vh2) = g.forward(toks[pos], pos, kh, vh)
      kh := kh2
      vh := vh2
      losses := losses.addRight(nll(logits, toks[pos + 1]))
    end
    loss = (BIG OPLUS[l <- losses] l) / (n 1.0)
    backward(loss)
    lrT = lr0 (1.0 - (step 1.0) / (numSteps 1.0))
    for i <- seq(0#nP) do
      p = params[i]
      g1 = p.grad
      g2 = g1 g1

      vBuf[i] := beta2 vBuf[i] + (1.0 - beta2) g2

      p.grad := 0.0
      p.visited := false
    end
    if (step + 1) REM 10 = 0 then do
      el = (((nanoTime() - t0) + 500000) DIV 1000000)
      println("step " (step + 1) " / " numSteps "  loss " loss.data "  elapsed " el " ms")
    end end
  end

  (* inference: temperature sampling *)
  temp = 0.5
  println("--- inference ---")
  for s <- seq(1#10) do
    var kh: List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] := emptyHist(nHead)
    var vh: List[\List[\List[\V\]\]\] := emptyHist(nHead)
    var tid: ZZ32 := bos
    var out: String := ""
    var stop: Boolean := false
    for pos <- seq(0#blockSize) do
      if NOT stop then
        (logits, kh2, vh2) = g.forward(tid, pos, kh, vh)
        kh := kh2
        vh := vh2
        probs = softmax(logits / temp)
        r = random(1.0)
        var cum: RR64 := 0.0
        var pick: ZZ32 := vocab - 1
        var done: Boolean := false
        for i <- seq(0#vocab) do
          if NOT done then
            cum := cum + probs[i].data
            if r < cum then pick := i; done := true end
          end
        end
        if pick = bos then stop := true
        else out := out || char(pick + 97); tid := pick end
      end
    end
    println("sample " s ": " out)
  end
end
end

## Notation contests, and how each was adjudicated

### 1. Vector·matrix as `opr juxtaposition` — **blocked by the interpreter; ⊞ adopted**

The spec's point 2 asks for `opr juxtaposition(p: List[\V\], m:
List[\List[\V\]\])` coexisting with the existing matrix·vector overload. The
interpreter refuses, verbatim:

```
com.sun.fortress.exceptions.ProgramError: .../pprobe.fss:48:1-49:70: and
.../pprobe.fss:45:1-46:65:
first parameters p:[List[\V\],List[\List[\V\]\]] and w:[List[\List[\V\]\],List[\V\]] are unrelated (neither subtype, excludes, nor equal) and no excluding pair is present
Context:
.../pprobe.fss:48:1-49:70:
.../pprobe.fss:5:1-18:2:
```

This is a **known, in-tree-documented limitation**, not a mistake of ours.
`ProjectFortress/tests/doubledOverloading3.fss` records the same error with
the comment: *"A parametric type can't have a functional method right now,
because we end up with top-level overloadings that aren't provably disjoint.
But we've ruled out multiple extension of a single type a different
parameterizations (right?), so we should consider these instantiations to be
disjoint (right right?)."* Two distinct instantiations of the same generic
trait (`List[\V\]` vs `List[\List[\V\]\]`) are treated as *possibly
overlapping* rather than excluding, and Fortress's overload rule then demands
that at least one parameter position exclude — which it never does here,
because both positions are List instantiations.

The consequence is sharper than "one overload failed": **at most one
overload of any given operator can be declared on (List, List).** Vec·Vec,
Mat·Vec and Vec·Mat are pairwise unrelated in exactly this way, so the same
error appears for every pairing, and `DOT` cannot absorb the vector·matrix
product either (checked by the same reasoning: position 0 is `List[\V\]` in
both, position 1 is the unrelated pair). Three products need three distinct
names.

Alternatives considered:

- give **matrix·vector** the second name and keep `p M` as juxtaposition —
  rejected: `W x` occurs seven times in `forward` (wq/wk/wv/wo/fc1/fc2/lmHead)
  against one occurrence of `p V`, and `W x` is the more universal paper form;
- **transpose**: `attend(q, K, Vv) = Vv^T softmax(…)`, which needs only
  matrix·vector — rejected: `p V = (Vᵀ p)` is true but it inverts the paper's
  own reading order and adds an O(n·d) transpose that is pure implementation
  accident;
- **a second big operator over the vector carrier** — adopted.

Adopted form:

```
attend(q: List[\V\], K: List[\List[\V\]\], Vv: List[\List[\V\]\]): List[\V\] = do
  p = softmax(<|[\V\] ((q DOT k) / SQRT |q|) | k <- K|>)
  BIG BOXPLUS[j <- 0#|p|] p[j] Vv[j]
end
```

which renders as `⊞_{j←0#|p|} pⱼ Vvⱼ` — i.e. **the brief's own target
formula, `Output_i = Σⱼ Softmax(A_i)ⱼ · Vⱼ`**, with ⊞ where the paper prints
Σ. It uses the scalar·vector juxtaposition the spec asked for, and the
"second-monoid problem" the journal worried about turns out to be a
*naming* problem only: a second nullary `BIG OPLUS()` registration does
collide, but a registration under a **different glyph** does not. The
vector-carrier reduction (`vecsum` + `VecConcat` + `opr BIG BOXPLUS`) is a
literal transposition of the scalar ⊕ design — map to singletons, join by
concatenation (exactly associative), fold once componentwise at the leaf —
and produces the identical graph to `microgpt_native`'s index comprehension:
one n-ary Sum node per output component, the same multiply nodes underneath.

Recording this as a language finding: **the register we wanted is expressible;
what blocks it is the 2012 overload checker's inability to see two
instantiations of an invariant generic as disjoint.** That is a concrete,
minimal repro for a future compiler-gap catalog entry (and it already has an
in-tree test file waiting for it).

### 2. `DOT` vs juxtaposition for the inner product — **DOT**

`u DOT v` renders as `u · v`, exactly the papers' inner-product dot, and it
keeps juxtaposition free for the matrix·vector product (which by contest 1 is
a scarce resource: one List-List overload per name). It also gives `rmsnorm`
its ‖x‖² directly: `x DOT x`.

Coexistence checked: the library already has `opr DOT(self, b: Number): RR64`
on `Number`, and a top-level `opr DOT(List[\V\], List[\V\])` overloads it
without complaint — trait-vs-trait exclusion works between `List` and
`Number`; it is only same-generic instantiations that fail.

### 3. Named function vs operator for softmax / rmsnorm / concat — **named, as the literature names them**

The literature prints `softmax`, `RMSNorm`, `concat`, `relu`, `FFN` as named
operators-in-words, and Fortify sets them in italic exactly that way. No
contest survived the render: `rmsnorm(x) = x/√((x·x)/|x| + 0.00001)` next to
the paper's `RMSNorm(x) = x/√(x·x/d + ε)` is a one-glyph difference.

### 4. `^0.5` vs `√` — **√, via `opr SQRT(u: V)`**

The spec writes `rmsnorm(x) = x / (((x DOT x)/(d) + eps)^0.5)`. Rendered,
`^0.5` is visibly not the paper. Defining `opr SQRT(u: V): V = u^0.5`
(one line, and its own exhibit of "what Fortress must be taught") turns the
model line into the radical the paper prints. Same for the attention scale:
`/ SQRT |q|`.

### 5. The ZZ32→RR64 coercion blemishes — **pushed down into the notation layer**

The journal flagged `d 1.0`-style coercions as known blemishes of
`microgpt_native`. Fortress does not coerce `ZZ32` to `RR64` implicitly, so
they cannot simply be deleted; they can be *quarantined*. Three one-line
declarations do it, and they belong on the "what Fortress must be taught"
side of the exhibit rather than in the formulas:

```
opr /(self, n: ZZ32): V = self / (n 1.0)      (* inside V *)
opr +(self, c: RR64): V = ...                 (* inside V *)
opr SQRT(n: ZZ32): RR64 = SQRT (n 1.0)
```

Result: `(x DOT x) / |x| + 0.00001` and `(q DOT k) / SQRT |q|` at the model
level, with no `1.0` multiplications and no `konst(…)` wrappers anywhere in
the rendered formulas. `d = |x|` and `dk = |q|` bindings disappeared too —
`|x|` is the paper's own notation for the dimension.

### 6. `Vv` for the value matrix — **kept, under protest, because `V` is taken**

Probed: a parameter named `V` is rejected outright (`Variable V is already
declared.`) since `V` is the autodiff object. `Vv` renders as a slightly
product-like "Vv", which is the same cost the journal recorded for `xa`/`xb`.
No better single glyph exists that is not already the engine's type name; the
spec had already chosen `Vv` for this reason and I kept it.

### 7. The forward-pass locals — **renamed to `K` and `Vv`, which fixed a LaTeX bug too**

`microgpt_native`'s `kh2`/`vh2` names produce `\VAR{kh}_2_{h}` in Fortify's
output, which is a **LaTeX "Double subscript" error** — the native sheet
silently carries it (it renders as `kh₂ₕ`, which means nothing). Renaming the
extended histories to `K` and `Vv` removes the error *and* makes the line
read as the paper does: `heads = ⟨attend(wq_h x₂, K_h, Vv_h) | h ← 0#nHead⟩`.
Flagging this as a defect in the existing `microgpt-native-forms.tic` too.

### 8. `softmax`'s max shift — **the `konst` wrapper dropped**

`c = konst(BIG MAX[u <- seq(a)] u.data)` became `c = BIG MAX[u <- seq(a)]
u.data`, an `RR64`, with `opr -(x: List[\V\], c: RR64)` doing the shift. This
is decision 5 of the journal taken at face value (the shift *is* an RR64
constant), it renders one node cleaner, and it changes the graph only by
removing a `konst` leaf and a negation node — values and gradients identical,
golden re-verified.

`u.data` in the `BIG MAX` stays: it is the honest marker of the one place the
formula steps outside the graph to read a number.

### 9. `nll` — **two lines beat one**

`-(log ((softmax(logits))[y]))` renders with a bracketed subscript and three
nested parens. Binding `p = softmax(logits)` first lets Fortify render `p[y]`
as `p_y`, giving `−(log(p_y))` — the paper's `L = −log softmax(logits)_y`.

`fc2 relu(fc1 x)` needs none of the spec's defensive parens
(`fc2 (relu (fc1 x))`): tight juxtaposition resolves `relu(fc1 x)` as an

The three from the prior report (chained subscripts need `(m[i])[j]`,
comprehension bodies ending in a subscript need parens, list-literal type

24	   n-ary Sum node built by BIG OPLUS over a list-concatenation monoid),
25	   the tokenizer, Adam, the training loop and the sampling loop carry over
26	   from microgpt_native.fss unchanged.  Adam stays index-form RR64

28	   arithmetic, and the contrast with the model level is a teaching point.

31	   vector-times-matrix "opr juxtaposition(p: List[\V\], m: List[\List[\V\]\])"
32	   alongside the matrix-times-vector one, so that the attention blend reads
33	   "softmax(...) Vv".  The interpreter rejects the pair:
34	
35	     first parameters p:[List[\V\],List[\List[\V\]\]] and

41	   this limitation, and doubts it in its own comment).  Consequence: at most
42	   one overload of any operator may be declared on (List, List), so Vec.Vec,
43	   Mat.Vec and Vec.Mat need three different names.  DOT takes the inner
44	   product, juxtaposition takes W x (seven uses against one), and the blend
45	   becomes a reduction under its own glyph:  BIG BOXPLUS[j] p[j] Vv[j],
46	   which is the brief's target formula Output_i = SUM_j softmax(A_i)_j V_j
47	   with (+) boxed.  The second-monoid worry turns out to be per-NAME, not

## Summary

`explorations/microgpt_paper.fss` (416 lines) implements the paper-register spec, and `explorations/fortify/microgpt-paper-forms.tic` typesets it. All three gates pass on the exact delivered file.

**Gates** (`FORTRESS_THREADS=1`, three full runs — first draft, post-render-edit, as delivered):

| gate | result |
|---|---|
| goldenCheck at 1e-9 | PASS first attempt, and on every later run; 1264 params, identical to `microgpt_native` and v1 |
| 30-step nano run | PASS all three — delivered file 3.212 → 2.568, opening band = ln 27 |
| timing | **4.62 s/step** (138.6 s / 30) vs `microgpt_native`'s 4.81 — the notation layer costs nothing |

**The one spec item that could not be built.** The spec's vector×matrix `opr juxtaposition(p: List[\V\], m: List[\List[\V\]\])` is rejected by the interpreter: *"first parameters p:[List[\V\],List[\List[\V\]\]] and w:[List[\List[\V\]\],List[\V\]] are unrelated (neither subtype, excludes, nor equal) and no excluding pair is present."* Two instantiations of the same generic trait aren't seen as disjoint — the in-tree `ProjectFortress/tests/doubledOverloading3.fss` records exactly this and doubts it in its own comment. The sharper consequence: **at most one overload of any operator may be declared on (List, List)**, so Vec·Vec, Mat·Vec and Vec·Mat need three different names. `DOT` takes the inner product, juxtaposition takes `W x` (seven uses against one), and the blend becomes `BIG BOXPLUS[j <- 0#|p|] p[j] Vv[j]` — which renders as ⊞ⱼ pⱼVⱼ, i.e. the brief's own target formula `Output_i = Σⱼ Softmax(A_i)ⱼ · Vⱼ`. A useful side finding: the "second monoid collides" worry is per-*name*, not per-carrier — a second nullary `BIG OPLUS()` collides, a `BIG BOXPLUS()` does not.

**Render-driven iterations** (three passes, each re-gated): dropped `konst` from softmax's shift; split `nll` so Fortify renders `p_y` instead of a bracketed subscript; renamed `kh2`/`vh2` to `K`/`Vv`, which also fixed a real LaTeX "Double subscript" error — **verified to be present in the committed `microgpt-native-forms.tic` too**; and pushed the ZZ32→RR64 coercions down into the notation layer so `rmsnorm(x) = x / √((x·x)/|x| + 0.00001)` and `ffn(x) = fc₂ relu(fc₁ x)` carry no `1.0` multiplications. Two blemishes remain, both Fortify's: the `opr SQRT(u: V)` declaration sets its parameter under the radical, and the `__bigOperatorSugar` registration is a wall of type arguments — kept deliberately, since that line is the price of teaching Fortress a second reduction.

**New syntax traps:** `|w||>` and `/|` don't lex (need a space); `V` can't be reused as a variable name while the object `V` is in scope (`K` is fine).
